options: A synonym for an availability zone
A single physical server located anywhere in the world
A billing category with no relationship to physical location
A set of datacenters in one geographic area, connected by a low-latency network
questions.explain: A region is a geography — like East US or West Europe — made up of multiple datacenters connected by a low-latency network.

options: A virtual, software-only construct with no physical datacenter behind it
The same physical building as every other zone in the region
A separate country entirely outside the region
A physically separate datacenter within a region, with its own power, cooling, and networking
questions.explain: Availability zones are physically separate datacenters inside one region, so a failure in one (power, cooling) doesn't affect the others.

questions.q: Why does spreading a resource across multiple availability zones improve resilience?
options: It automatically encrypts all data at rest
It makes the resource run faster in every scenario
It removes the need to ever choose a region
A failure in one zone's datacenter — like a power or cooling outage — doesn't take down the others
questions.explain: Because each zone has its own power, cooling, and networking, one zone's failure doesn't cascade into the others.

questions.q: Why does latency matter when choosing a region?
options: Latency only affects storage costs, not response times
Latency is only a concern for on-premises servers, never for the cloud
A user far from the chosen region will see slower response times than one located near it
All Azure regions have identical latency to every location on Earth
questions.explain: Placing resources near the users who will actually use them reduces the round-trip delay of every request.

questions.q: What is data residency, and why can it force a specific region choice?
options: A marketing term with no real compliance implications
A setting that has nothing to do with where a resource is deployed
A requirement that certain data physically remain within a specific country or region's borders, sometimes due to law
A guarantee that data is always duplicated in every Azure region worldwide
questions.explain: Some organizations and laws require data to stay within a country or region's borders, which can force a specific region choice regardless of user location.
